practice.prompt: "Man könnte argumentieren, dass …" is best used to:
choices: introduce a claim tentatively, without stating it as flat fact

practice.prompt: "Es wäre denkbar, dass …" is even more tentative than "man könnte argumentieren" because it:
choices: only flags an idea as possible, without arguing for it
is only used in spoken German
asserts the idea is definitely true

practice.prompt: "Es ließe sich sagen, dass …" builds on which earlier construction?

choices: a counterargument the writer will go on to address

practice.prompt: "Es wäre zu fragen, ob …" combines Konjunktiv II with which earlier pattern?
In "Es mag sein, dass die Lösung teuer ist, aber sie ist sinnvoll," what is "mag"?
choices: the plain indicative of mögen, used for a concession
the Konjunktiv I "möge" from B2 Unit 9

practice.prompt: "Der Einwand ist nicht von der Hand zu weisen" means the objection is:
choices: hard to dismiss — it deserves to be taken seriously
the writer's own opinion, stated directly

practice.prompt: How does this unit's hedged Konjunktiv II differ from B2 Unit 9's Konjunktiv I?
choices: This unit softens the writer's OWN argument; Unit 9 reports someone ELSE's claim
They are exactly the same construction
Unit 9 is only used in speaking
This unit is only used for questions

practice.prompt: How does this unit's hedging differ from B1 Unit 8's "dürfte"/"müsste"?
choices: Both voice the speaker's own view, but this unit's phrases specifically hedge an ARGUMENT, not a factual guess
There is no difference at all
dürfte can never appear in an essay
This unit's phrases are only used for weather forecasts

practice.prompt: "Man sollte diesen Einzelfall nicht verallgemeinern" is a caution against:
choices: drawing a general conclusion from a single case

quiz.prompt: "Man könnte argumentieren, dass die Reform zu spät kommt." — what is the effect of "könnte" here?
choices: it softens the claim into a tentative possibility rather than a flat assertion
it makes the sentence a direct command
it turns the sentence into a question
it has no effect on meaning

quiz.prompt: Which is the most tentative of these three hedges?
"Es ließe sich behaupten, dass beide Positionen extrem sind." — "ließe sich" comes from which verb?
"Man könnte einwenden, dass die Kosten zu hoch wären." is typically followed, in a well-structured essay, by:
choices: the writer addressing or responding to that objection
a direct quotation from the objector

quiz.prompt: "Es wäre zu fragen, ob diese Zahlen überhaupt vergleichbar sind." — which earlier B1 construction does "wäre zu fragen" build on?
"Man könnte meinen, das Problem sei gelöst — tatsächlich ist es nur verschoben." — what does the second half do?
choices: overturns the first impression the hedge set up
confirms the first impression is correct
repeats the same claim in other words

quiz.prompt: "Es mag sein, dass nicht jeder zustimmt, aber die Fakten sprechen für sich." — which half carries the writer's real, firmer point?
"Der Einwand ist nicht von der Hand zu weisen" — what kind of expression is this?
"Es ist fraglich, ob diese Maßnahme ausreicht." — is Konjunktiv II required here?
choices: No — "fraglich" already signals doubt in the plain indicative
Only if the sentence is negative

quiz.prompt: "So könnte man sagen, dass beide Ansätze ihre Berechtigung haben." most naturally appears:
choices: closing a paragraph, tying threads together tentatively
as the very first sentence of an essay

quiz.prompt: Which tool reports what SOMEONE ELSE said, rather than softening the writer's own argument?
choices: B2 Unit 9's Konjunktiv I (er sagte, er komme)

quiz.prompt: "Diese Zahl muss man relativieren: sie stammt aus einer kleinen Stichprobe." — what is the writer doing?
choices: qualifying the figure's significance rather than rejecting it outright

quiz.prompt: "Beide Standpunkte haben etwas für sich." — "der Standpunkt" means:
"Sein Ärger ist nachvollziehbar, auch wenn ich ihm nicht zustimme." — "nachvollziehbar" signals:
choices: understanding the logic of a claim without necessarily agreeing with it
